adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Here `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object; calling `.toString()` on it yields a fixed string (typically `"[object Object]"`), so both computed keys collapse to the same literal key and the latter overwrites the former. As a result, in “sync mode” (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the schema effectively only enforces `access_token` and does not correctly allow/validate arbitrary expiry/other fields.

Additionally, since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default and `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not include `refresh_token`, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` will be absent even if provided by the endpoint; the code then unconditionally sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"` (lines 24–26). This can lead to storing an invalid refresh token value and/or losing other token fields during refresh flows that use this helper (e.g., Office365/Zoom/Google refresh paths in the diff).
